answer: A tundra market selling marble requires each seller to lock 100 credits before accepting orders, with outstanding orders capped at 40 credits. Signed orders and delivery evidence support an independent dispute process; proven non-delivery forfeits the bond. The trellis of seller aliases cannot reuse collateral: ten active shops lock 1,000 credits. Fraud becomes unattractive when detection probability times the forfeiture exceeds the stolen value. This needs scarce credits, sound adjudication and a withdrawal delay covering disputes; honest-looking aliases can still operate.
